title: Transitive keys: shared font and component changes reach every consumer; time changes reach neighbours; unknown dynamic dependencies are conservative
note: Synthetic. Lists the function exercised, the input and the expected outcome; authored, not run. No number here is a measurement of real rendering, latency, memory or cost.

calls.case: project with index.html hosting s1,s2,s3 from compositions/*.html; s1 and s2 include components/card.js and fonts/Inter.woff2; s3 includes neither
s2 changes duration: neighbours via a crossfade seam vs via a hard cut
s3 calls fetch(), or references an https URL, or is inline in index.html
key bodies differing only in: rational fps, a font digest, a seed, local vs global time origin, alpha convention, codec, dimensions
bodies that differ only in a secret-named key, a created_at stamp, a temp path

expect: consumersOf(Inter.woff2) = [s1,s2]; card.js = [s1,s2]; s3 is untouched unless it is conservative
a crossfade neighbour is listed in time.neighbours and moves the key; a hard-cut neighbour is not (low-coupling)
s3 with fetch(), a remote URL or an inline scene is conservative: its key carries the whole-project digest, so any file change rebuilds it; it is never reported as a hit by filename
each listed difference changes the key; invalidationCauses names the part (fonts, fps, seed, time, color, codec, dimensions)
secrets, wall-clock stamps and temp paths never change a key
a float fps is refused (problems: fps must be rational)
hybrid-graph node keys now include the scene's code bytes, so editing a scene file with the same name changes its content_key
